FN-Y8I96N6-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 63
Committee: County and Municipal Government Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/05/2025
Senate Bill 63 as introduced would increase the obligations of law enforcement agencies, by an
undetermined amount, to: (1) collect fingerprints and DNA samples on all illegal aliens in
custody prior to release; and (2) submit the fingerprints to the Alabama Law Enforcement
Agency and the DNA samples to the Alabama Department of Forensic Sciences.
This would increase the obligations of (1) the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency to receive and
enter into the appropriate database fingerprints received from law enforcement agencies; and (2)
the Alabama Department of Forensic Sciences to conduct DNA analysis of samples received by
local law enforcement agencies entered into the appropriate DNA database. However, any
increased obligations to the Department would be offset, beginning in fiscal year 2026, by the
increase in the DNA Database Fund fee distribution from the current amount of $11 to $14
assessed in all municipal, district and circuit court criminal cases, bond forfeiture proceedings,
and certain arrest warrants.

FN-Y8I96N6-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 63
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/18/2025
Senate Bill 63 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of law enforcement agencies,
by an undetermined amount, to: (1) collect fingerprints and DNA samples on all illegal aliens in
custody prior to release; and (2) submit the fingerprints to the Alabama Law Enforcement
Agency (ALEA) and the DNA samples to the Alabama Department of Forensic Sciences.
This bill would increase the obligations of ALEA and the department by an undetermined
amount, respectively, to: (1) receive and enter into the appropriate database fingerprints received
from law enforcement agencies; and (2) conduct DNA analysis of samples received by local law
enforcement agencies entered into the appropriate DNA database. However, any increased
obligations to the department would be offset, in whole or in part, beginning in fiscal year 2026,
by an additional estimated $1.8 million annually deposited into the DNA Database Fund by
increasing the court cost amount deposited into the fund from $11, under current law, to $14, as
provided by this bill.
